title: Verification
description: One verifier's verdicts on every merged finding of one batch, written independently of the other verifiers and without knowledge of labels (protocol.md section 5, verify protocol). Semantic check in panel.py: no_trigger_reason is non-null when the merged finding's trigger or wrong_output is null.

verdict.description: confirm: the failure scenario was reproduced or traced and no reason the code is correct was found. refute: a documented regime, caller precondition, convention or derivation shows the code is correct, or the trigger cannot occur. uncertain: correctness turns on an assumption the code and its documentation do not settle (named in deciding_assumption), or the scenario could not be established.

evidence.description: How the verdict was established. reproduced: the trigger was run (python3 -B or node) and its output observed. traced: the trigger was followed line by line through the code, with the lines named in reason. none: neither. A confirm with evidence none counts as uncertain.

refutation_search.description: Where the verifier looked for a reason the code is correct before deciding: the files, callers, docstrings and conventions read, and what each showed.

reach.description: Files read to establish how the trigger state arises (configuration, environment, deployment, release) and what each showed; 'none present' when the project has none.

trigger_class.description: How the trigger state comes about. unreachable only with verdict refute.

possibly_intended.description: The behaviour looks like a deliberate, undocumented trade-off. Not allowed with refute; counts as uncertain.

possibly_intended_reason.description: Required and non-empty when possibly_intended is true; null otherwise.

value_corrections.description: Quoted values the repository contradicts; empty when none.

reproduction.description: The code or command run to reproduce the failure, with its observed output, so that a reader can run it; required when evidence is reproduced, null otherwise.

extent.description: A few runs, input by input, including ordinary inputs that are handled correctly, so that a reader sees which inputs fail; empty when the verifier ran none.

in_practice_revision.description: A full replacement for the finding's in_practice statement, when your reach contradicts or omits part of it (for example a trigger the finder ruled out); null when the statement stands.

ValueCorrection.description: A value quoted in the finding that the repository contradicts.

ExtentRow.description: One run: an input, the result it should give and the result the code gives.
